messages.subject: Any Alternatives to Univariate Sampling ?
parts:
I have been attempting to run the following model. I am encountering problems when the dimension of tau[1:Q] increases.


spatNimCode <- nimbleCode({
  
  for (m in 1:M){
    for (r in 1:R){
        y[m,r] ~ dcat(prob[r,m,1:K])
      }}
  
  for (m in 1:M){  
    for (r in 1:R){ 
        for (k in 1:K){  
          eta[r,m,k] <- theta[map.to.theta[r]] - beta[m,k] 
          psum[r,m,k] <- sum(eta[r,m,1:k])
          exp.psum[r,m,k] <- exp(psum[r,m,k])
          prob[r,m,k] <- exp.psum[r,m,k]/sum(exp.psum[r,m,1:K])
        }}}
  
  theta[1:Bmax] <- bgcovs[1:Bmax,1:6] %*% alpha_theta[1:6] + Mop[1:Bmax,1:Q] %*% tau[1:Q]
  
  tau[1:Q] ~ dmnorm(mu_tau[1:Q],prec=Sigma_tau[1:Q,1:Q]) 
  
  Sigma_tau[1:Q,1:Q] <- Qs[1:Q,1:Q]*sigmasq
  
  for (m in 1:M){
    beta[m,1] <- 0
    for (k in 2:K){
      beta[m,k] ~ dnorm(0,sd=1)
    }
  }
  sigmasq ~ dgamma(.5,scale=2000)
  for (t in 1:6){ alpha_theta[t] ~ dnorm(0,sd=9) }
 
  
})



For Q <= 10, I am able to run the model successfully using the default RW_block sampler (I do receive the message ‘void sampler _RW_block:: adaptiveProcedure(bool)). As soon as   Q > 10, using RW_block fails when I attempt to build the MCMC with the error message: object ‘propCovHistory’ not found.


If I use univariate samplers for the elements of tau, I can get the model to work again. However, it takes a very long time. For Q=50, it took 3 days. I have also attempted to use the AF_slice, but this just resulted in errors as well.


At first, I thought perhaps the behavior of the RW_block sampler with regards to adapting the propCov might be the problem. However, it is my understanding that the default behavior for the propCov is to not allow adaption. I assumed (perhaps wrongly) that the message I received for Q <=10 was indicating the scale was being fixed to 1.


Realistically, Q = 50 is the smallest value that would be useful. Is there another sampler or a change I can make in the default settings of the two samplers I have tried that would enable me to run this model in a more timely manner? Any suggestions would be much appreciated. 


I have attached two data sets: one with Q=10 and one with Q=50 as well as the code associated with running the model. 


Thanks,


Kori

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Any Alternatives to Univariate Sampling ?
parts:
Apologies, Kori.  This error is related to recent changes to the RW_block sampler, which allow for saving the adaptation parameters through the course of a run (for diagnostic purposes), but instead has resulted in some errors in your case.

I've just made some changes on our development branch of NIMBLE, to this problem.  Until the next release, which will include these fixes, you can install from our development branch using:

remove.packages('nimble')
library(devtools)
install_github('nimble-dev/nimble', ref = 'devel', subdir = 'packages/nimble')
library(nimble)

This should solve the problem you're having, with using the RW_block sampler when Q > 10.

Please let us know if this works for you, now.

Cheers!
Daniel
